text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-A Moroccan shipping agent says there is a professional unit helping Moroccan stowaways on ships sailing to Norway and Europe.
-Norway's Nobel Institute has received a total of 130 nominations for this year's Peace Price, the highest number ever nominated. Twenty-five of the nominees are organisations.
-Eastern European contries and Asia are becoming more important markets for Norwegian exports. Exports to the European Union, however, declined in 1996, statistics show.

-A possible merger between Norway's two largest commercial banks, Den norske Bank and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, could lead to a higher value for the shares in both, American brokerage Salomon Brothers says.

-Scandinavian Airlines Systems posted a 31 percent fall in pre-tax profits in 1996. The airliner said stronger competition could continue to hit revenues in 1997, but it still expected this year's results to be in line with last year.
